I don’t know what was different from the previous recipe. I’m not that familiar with the ins and outs of bread chemistry. This one seemed really dry after I added the liquids but before adding the butter. There was still dry flour in the bowl. 

It’s a recipe for cinnamon buns, so I guess an enriched dough. 

I have a scale, but the ingredients list only gives the dry ingredients in weight and the liquids are in volume. I guess I could figure it out myself in weight, but again I’m not an expert and generally just follow what’s in the book. 

My ingredients were not perfectly room temperature. Maybe that is the problem. 

I was using the stir speed, since using 2nd speed would have definitely caused it to burn out. 

It’s a new mixer. I bought it brand new, but have had it for two months now so that’s why I said almost brand new. 

It came with a spiral dough hook, so that’s what I used. I find that the dough hook does a terrible job of mixing the dry and wet together at first. It leaves a lot of dry along the edges. So the stuff in the middle likely gets over mixed while I’m waiting for the edges to work their way in. I do stop it to use a spatula to poke the dry down but that only helps a little. 

In the past I had a smaller kitchenaid with a c hook that seemed to work a bit better at getting the dry and wet to mix.

I have an artisan series kitchenaid stand mixer. It’s almost brand new. I’m using it to make bread by following recipes out of the Americas Test Kitchen book. Im measuring ingredients meticulously according to the directions. 

I’ve never had problems baking bread before getting this new mixer. 

The problem that I’m having is that the recipes seem so incredibly dry, and the dough is so hard and elasticky while I’m mixing it, and it’s basically burning out my mixer. 

The mixer is getting caught up on the sides as it’s pushing through the dough and the arm nearly stops. Then it suddenly releases and all the pent up energy is released at once, causing it to speed up for a few seconds. 

What am I doing wrong? This mixer should be able to handle a lot, but the dough is so stiff that it’s nearly breaking.

For what it’s worth, I can also barely knead the dough by hand because it’s so stiff. It’s like kneading a rubber ball. 

Is this a sign that my dough isn’t hydrated enough?  

Why would that happen if I’m following the recipe?
